acne.note: Uncountable: bad acne, a lot of acne (not "an acne").
ex: Many teenagers have problems with acne at school.
This cream helps to treat acne on your face.
Stress and bad sleep can make your acne worse.
He went to a doctor about his acne last week.

limousine.note: Often shortened to "limo" in informal English.

ex: I use an electric mixer to make cakes.
Our new kitchen mixer is very loud.
The DJ turned up the sound on the mixer.
Put the eggs and sugar in the mixer.
The auditor checked all the company's accounts.
An auditor from another company checks our finances every year.
She works as an auditor for a big firm.
The auditors found several mistakes in the report.
The pasta was served with black truffle and cheese.
Dogs can find truffles under the ground in forests.
Real truffles are very expensive in most stores.
She ordered fries with truffle oil at the cafe.

old-school.note: Informal: old-fashioned, often in a good or cool way.
ex: He has an old-school way of teaching math.
I really love old-school hip-hop from the nineties.
Writing letters by hand feels very old-school now.
My grandpa still uses an old-school phone with buttons.
She has worked in show business for many years.
It is very hard to get a job in show business.
He left show business to become a school teacher.
Many young people dream of a career in show business.

home office.note: A room at home where you work. For the way of working, say "work from home".
ex: I work from my home office three days a week.
He set up a small home office in the bedroom.
My home office has a big desk and a window.
A quiet home office helps me focus on work.
We need to improve our business processes this year.
This software makes the business process much faster.
Every business process in the company should be clear.
She helps big companies change their business processes.
She was on a cooking reality show last year.
I don't watch reality shows on TV anymore.
The new reality show is filmed on an island.
He became famous after winning a reality show.
The show is on TV during prime time on Thursdays.
Ads during prime time are very expensive.
Most families watch TV together in prime time.
The best shows usually start in prime time.

wild card.note: Also a person or thing you cannot predict: "He is a wild card."
ex: The team got a wild card to play in the tournament.
She entered the tennis tournament with a wild card.
The wild card team surprised everyone and won the title.
He received a wild card for the big race.

tight end.note: A player position in American football.
ex: The tight end caught the ball and ran forward.
He plays tight end for his college football team.
Our tight end blocked well during the whole game.
The tight end scored a touchdown in the last minute.

boy scout.note: Often written "Boy Scout"; can also mean a very honest, good man.
ex: My son became a boy scout this year.
The boy scouts went camping in the forest.
He was a boy scout when he was a kid.
The boy scouts helped clean the park on Saturday.

blah blah blah.note: Informal; used to skip boring talk.
ex: He talked about work all evening, blah blah blah.
She said she was sorry again, blah blah blah.
It's always the same boring speech, blah blah blah.
My boss talked about rules and deadlines, blah blah blah.
My grandparents do tai chi in the park every morning.
Tai chi is slow, quiet, and very relaxing.
She takes a tai chi class on Mondays.
Doctors say tai chi helps older people with balance.
Please send me a pro forma invoice first.
The bank needs a pro forma budget for next year.
We got the pro forma invoice by email yesterday.
This meeting is just pro forma, so nothing will change.

a priori.note: Formal word, used mostly in science and philosophy.

know-how.note: Uncountable: practical skill and knowledge, not an invention (not "a know-how").

check-in.note: The verb is two words: "check in at the hotel".
ex: Hotel check-in starts at three o'clock.
The airport check-in was very slow today.
You can do online check-in a day early.
We waited in line at the check-in desk.

buy-in.note: In business, "buy-in" often means support: "We need buy-in from the team."

jasmine.note: Often a girl's name, "Jasmine"; as a plant: "jasmine tea", "jasmine rice".
ex: The garden smells of jasmine in the evening.
Can I have a cup of jasmine tea, please?
White jasmine grows next to our front door.
This candle has a sweet jasmine smell.
He was born into a family of aristocrats.
The old aristocrat lived in a huge castle.
Many aristocrats lost their land after the revolution.
She acts like an aristocrat, but her family is poor.

bluff.note: Often a verb: "Is he bluffing?" "Bluff" can also mean a high, steep bank by a river.
ex: His big bet in the poker game was just a bluff.
I knew his threat to leave was only a bluff.
Is he serious, or is it a bluff?
Her angry message was a bluff to get a better price.

brunette.note: Mostly used for women; for men, "He has dark hair" is more usual.
ex: The brunette in the red coat is my sister.
She was a brunette, but now her hair is blond.
Two brunettes and a redhead came into the cafe.
The actress is a brunette with green eyes.

kilogram.note: Often shortened to "kilo" or "kg"; in the US people usually use pounds.

playboy.note: Also the name of a magazine; as a common noun: a rich man who lives for fun and parties.

iris.note: Often "iris" means the colored part of the eye around the pupil.

boycott.note: Also a verb: "to boycott a store".

ex: She reads her horoscope every morning with coffee.
My horoscope says I will have a lucky week.
Do you really believe in horoscopes and stars?
The magazine has a horoscope page at the back.
She is a columnist for a local newspaper.
The columnist writes about money and jobs every week.
I always read that columnist on Sundays.
The columnist got many angry letters from readers.

mod.note: Also short for "moderator", a person who controls a chat or forum.

cleaner.note: Often "cleaner" means more clean ("cleaner air") or a product: "glass cleaner".

jingle.note: Also the sound of small bells or keys: "the jingle of keys"; also a verb.

instrumental.note: Most often an adjective: "She was instrumental in our success" (she helped a lot).

ex: The new medicine is an inhibitor that slows the virus.
Rust inhibitors help protect the metal pipes.
This inhibitor stops the reaction from going too fast.
Scientists tested a new inhibitor in the lab.

light.note: Most often "light" means brightness: "Turn on the light." It also means not heavy.
ex: I'll have a light beer with my dinner, please.
Do you have light mayo for this sandwich?
This light yogurt has less sugar and fat.
She buys light cream cheese to eat healthier.
Turn on Bluetooth to connect the speaker.
My new headphones connect to my phone with Bluetooth.
The Bluetooth on my phone isn't working today.
Can you connect the keyboard through Bluetooth, please?
